title: VarNet cascade phase-view reconstruction screen
hypothesis: After training an official fastMRI VarNet on one synthetic multi-coil scanner, tying cascade denoisers loses quality on a held-out coil-sensitivity scanner, while a per-cascade complex Givens Mirror angle over one shared denoiser recovers more quality per serialized byte than hard tying and a same-count scalar-gate control, without changing the VarNet data-consistency parameters or acquired k-space operator.

data.type: deterministic analytic synthetic multi-coil phantoms; mechanism-only, not clinical or fastMRI benchmark evidence
data.train_scanner: A: fixed smooth coil profiles, train phantom seeds 106001..106032; first 24 train examples
data.target_scanner: B: shifted smooth coil amplitude and phase profiles; support seeds 106101..106108, development seeds 106201..106216

methods: independent native VarNet fine-tune on support upper control
shared single denoiser, no view (hard-tying baseline)
shared denoiser plus three per-cascade scalar gates
shared denoiser plus three per-cascade complex Givens angles (Mirror)
protocol.adaptation_scope: scanner sensitivity estimator and DC scalars remain frozen for all view methods; full native FT upper control may update all model parameters
protocol.view_placement: post-denoiser complex output only, before the native VarNetBlock sensitivity expansion and DC subtraction
protocol.dc_invariant: Mirror has no access to mask, acquired k-space values, or cascade dc_weight; report acquired-line residual for all methods. Native fastMRI VarNet uses learned soft DC, so exact measured-sample projection is not claimed.
protocol.selection: development seeds only; freeze all weights/codes before fresh seed access

paid_objects: independent per-cascade weights for native control

success_gate: Mirror improves hard-tying development NMSE by at least 10%, is within 5% relative NMSE of independent fine-tune, beats same-count scalar gates, uses at least 20% fewer actual total bytes than independent fine-tune, and does not alter VarNet DC parameters; fresh must confirm direction in all three worlds before PROMISING.
failure_gate: Mirror equals hard tying, is matched/dominated by the scalar gate, fails measurement-operator invariance, or its payload/runtime removes quality-per-byte benefit.
boundaries: Synthetic phantoms only; this is a VarNet mechanism screen, not fastMRI benchmark or clinical evidence.
No patient data or diagnosis tasks.
CPU small architecture; no full-scale VarNet latency claim.
No clinical or scanner deployment claim.
failure_gate_result: Amendment 01 fair tied pretraining: Givens Mirror NMSE 0.160418 vs hard tie 0.160539 (0.076% relative improvement), scalar gate 0.155246, independent FT 0.092474. Same serialized payload as scalar gate. Fresh remains sealed.

amendment_01.reason: The first development run exposed a control-init mismatch: independent cascades were trained first and then averaged to create the tied comparator. This is weaker than ordinary tying from initialization, so the initial screen is retained as exploratory only and a fairer rerun is frozen before the new metrics are read.
changes: Train an independent VarNet on the same Scanner-A examples for 24 updates.
Separately initialize a VarNet with one denoiser module shared across all three cascades from initialization, then train that hard-tied model on the same Scanner-A examples for 24 updates.
Initialize hard-tied, scalar-gate and Mirror target methods from this tied-pretrained state; keep scanner sensitivity model and per-cascade DC scalars unchanged for view-only methods.
Keep independent frozen and independent target full-fine-tune controls initialized from the independently pretrained model.
Use the already fixed Scanner-B 8-shot support and 16-row development sets. Fresh seeds remain sealed.

excluded_exploratory_run.reason: hard-tied model created by averaging independently trained cascades rather than ordinary tied pretraining
